Definition: Does the government maintain a digital civil register?
Comments: Digital civil registry pilot SIREC launched 2018 in Malabo capital only; operational but not expanded nationwide due to funding; 7 regional offices use manual paper processes; birth certificate coverage 65.7% per 2023 survey.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Fetched the World Bank Equatorial Guinea Digital Economy Diagnostic (2023, mirrored on openknowledge.worldbank.org), which confirms SIREC as a pilot digital civil registry launched by the Ministry of Justice in 2018 — consistent with 'Partially deployed'. No fresher evidence (searched to mid-2026) shows nationwide digital rollout, though a March 2025 decree appointing civil registrars across all provinces may indicate expansion of the physical (not necessarily digital) network. Value Code 4 confirmed; still single-sourced so recommend continued human corroboration.

Definition: Does the register cover births, deaths and marriages?
Comments: SIREC for new births and deaths; covers vital events.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited source itself only describes SIREC as covering births and deaths, not marriages, so it supports 'Some' rather than 'All'. A fresher INEGE Vital Facts report (presented Sept 2025, 2024 data) shows national vital statistics do include marriages and divorces, but it is unclear whether that data is captured through the digital SIREC register or separate paper/administrative channels. Given this conflict, code is reduced to 2 (Some) and flagged for human review to confirm whether marriages are captured digitally.

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: 65.7% population has birth certificate per 2023 national household survey (birth registration completeness proxy).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Equatorial Guinea's National Statistics Institute (INEGE) presented its second Vital Facts Report on 16 September 2025 (2024 data), reporting national birth registration coverage of 'just over 90%' (deaths also above 90%), up from the 65.7% (2023 survey) figure used originally. This fresher, primary, official source justifies raising the code from 3 (50-69%) to 5 (>89%).

Definition: What proportion of the electorate does the register cover?
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original comment cited only the absolute registered-voter count (419,817) with no denominator, from which '>89%' cannot be derived. International IDEA's Voter Turnout Database gives a 2022 voting-age population of 960,713, implying registration coverage of roughly 44% of the electorate; IFES Election Guide corroborates with ~427,671 registered against a total population of 1,679,172 (~25%). Both denominators place coverage in the 20-49% band, so the code is corrected from 5 to 2.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more tax registers?
Comments: Tax Identification Number (NIF) system exists and is mandatory per Tax Law No. 1/2024 for all economic actors.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original single source was a promotional LinkedIn post, an unreliable basis for 'Fully deployed nationwide'. Equatorial Guinea's Ley Tributaria and the Ministry of Finance's Ventanilla Única confirm a national fiscal register (NIF) exists for both individuals and businesses (Tax Law No. 1/2024, ratified 19 November 2024), but an April 2026 government announcement describes an ongoing rollout of a new digital tool for the business licence tax (Patente Tributaria) with tablets and scanners still being distributed to field teams as part of continuing modernisation. This indicates the system is being progressively digitised rather than fully deployed nationwide, so the code is revised from 5 to 4 (Partially deployed).

revision_notes: Confirmed via Equatorial Guinea's Ley Tributaria (Art. 27), which requires both natural persons (personas físicas) and legal entities (businesses) to register with the Fiscal Register (Registro Fiscal de contribuyentes), corroborating the PwC tax administration summary. Value Code 4 (Both income and business taxpayers) is confirmed.
